subject: Chemistry
title: Mendeleev Predicts Missing Elements
description: One-minute skill: Mendeleev Predicts Missing Elements.

hook.text: In 1869, Mendeleev arranged 63 elements by weight and left gaps—predicting elements that hadn't been found yet.

buildup.text: He noticed that properties repeat periodically when elements are ordered by atomic weight.

discovery.text: He left gaps for three undiscovered elements, predicting their atomic weights and chemical properties.

twist.text: Within 15 years, all three were found: gallium, scandium, and germanium—matching his predictions almost exactly.

climax.text: The periodic table became chemistry's most powerful organizing tool—and Mendeleev its greatest prophet.

punchline.text: Gaps in a table that predicted the future. Pattern recognition at its finest.

quiz.question: How did Mendeleev validate his periodic table?
options: He predicted properties of undiscovered elements that were later found to match
He synthesized three new elements in his laboratory
He proved that all elements are made of the same atom

details.summary: In 1869 Dmitri Mendeleev arranged elements by atomic weight and noticed periodic patterns in their properties, predicting the existence and properties of then-unknown elements. When gallium, scandium, and germanium were later discovered matching his predictions, the periodic table was validated.
details.whyItMatters: Mendeleev's predictions demonstrated that the periodic table was not just a catalog but a predictive scientific tool. It remains chemistry's most important organizational framework.
takeaways: Mendeleev left gaps in his table for undiscovered elements
He predicted properties of eka-aluminium, eka-boron, and eka-silicon
Discoveries of gallium and germanium closely matched his predictions

faq.question: How accurate were Mendeleev's predictions for unknown elements?
faq.answer: Remarkably accurate. For eka-aluminium, he predicted an atomic weight of 68, density of 5.9, and a low melting point. When gallium was discovered in 1875, its atomic weight was 69.7 and density 5.91. Similar accuracy held for germanium and scandium.

faq.question: Did anyone else create a periodic table before Mendeleev?
faq.answer: Several chemists noticed periodicity, including Newlands' Law of Octaves and Lothar Meyer's property curves. Mendeleev's key distinction was his willingness to leave gaps and make specific testable predictions. This boldness set his table apart from descriptive competitors.
